referrals.question: The plan defeats the warrant's purpose by prioritizing non-urgent storm-affected shipments (R1, R2, R3) over the time-critical medical shipment (U) that will fail its delivery deadline if express capacity is exhausted; this creates serious harm to urgent medical delivery duties that the warrant explicitly requires be preserved.

The plan defeats its own warrant purpose by filling express capacity with non-urgent shipments (R1, R2, R3—all non-time-critical, no need deadline) before attempting to serve the urgent shipment (U—medical supplies, 24-hour deadline, 12-hour express window). This leaves U unable to meet its critical deadline and violates the 'preserving urgent delivery duties' mandate. Rerouting R1, R2, R3 first is not authorized by the pending hold on U, which grants no exclusive seat and does not override the priority logic embedded in the warrant's purpose.

The plan's stated end ('Book supported storm shipments under current authority and resource limits') diverges fatally from the warrant's purpose ('Move storm-affected shipments while preserving urgent delivery duties'). Rerouting non-critical R1 before the pending time-critical U shipment inverts the priority hierarchy and risks failing the urgent duty. Moreover, U's pending hold is not exclusive permission—the resource policy explicitly states pending holds are not permission—so booking U now would violate the policy's one-seat-per-supported-demand rule until the hold settles at step 5. Proceeding with R1 before U's authority is settled creates a grave risk of displacing or delaying medical supplies that must arrive within 24 hours.
